name: Vasoproliferative Tumor of the Retina

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Vasoproliferative Tumor of the Retina

criteria.description: Presence of a solitary, pink-yellow elevated retinal mass typically located in the peripheral retina
Fluorescein angiography showing early hyperfluorescence with late leakage consistent with vascular proliferation
Ultrasound B-scan demonstrating a dome-shaped, acoustically solid retinal mass
Exclusion of other retinal tumors such as retinoblastoma or retinal hemangioblastoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical retinal mass with supportive imaging findings on fluorescein angiography and ultrasound
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy is rarely performed due to risk.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically pink-yellow in color and located in the inferotemporal quadrant
searchTerms: raised mass on edge of retina

pathognomonic.notes: Secondary to vascular leakage from the tumor

common.notes: Due to retinal edema or detachment

searchTerms: fluid or protein deposits inside or under retina
retinal exudates seen on eye exam

common.notes: May occur due to fragile tumor vessels
Visual distortion caused by retinal involvement

occasional.notes: Due to neovascularization or angle closure
Abnormal new vessel formation adjacent to tumor

rare.notes: Usually related to secondary glaucoma or inflammation
End-stage eye atrophy in untreated cases

imaging: Fluorescein angiography showing early hyperfluorescence and late leakage
Ultrasound B-scan demonstrating dome-shaped, acoustically solid retinal mass
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal thickening and subretinal fluid
other: Clinical examination revealing peripheral retinal mass with associated exudation
Fundus photography documenting lesion size and location

distinguishingFeatures: Typically occurs in children under 5 years
Leukocoria as a common presenting sign
Often associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease
Presence of dilated feeder and draining vessels

redFlags: Painful eye indicating secondary glaucoma or inflammation
Presence of vitreous hemorrhage obscuring fundus view
